title: The promotion-ready cutover suite was reduced to `:snapshot` alone, orphaning four operator instructions and removing the only remediation for a fix-pending Medium — with the archived code made uncompilable by design
fingerprintNote: Copied VERBATIM from classified-findings.json. NOT recomputed and NOT shortened by finding-manager. The fingerprint is the only collision-proof key for this record: the label is run-scoped and collides by name with pre-existing run-05 / run-21 / run-26 / run-27 `dev` ledger labels that are different findings.

entryPointBaseline.note: Delta scope for this record. entryPointBaselines.dev only — the project lastAuditedCommit (0e190e8) and branchBaselines.master were NOT the diff base and were NOT advanced by this run.

description:
At the diff base, `promotion-ready:snapshot`, `:dry`, `:broadcast`, `:resume` and `:verify` all existed. At HEAD only `:snapshot` survives (package.json:45). Four doc comments survive alongside it and still instruct operators to run the deleted keys — most explicitly `//order-of-execution:human-readable` at :46: "promotion-ready:snapshot then promotion-ready:dry then promotion-ready:broadcast. ... If the cutover fails, consult Claude on how to resume."

The underlying scripts were moved under `script/archives/`, which `foundry.toml:32` excludes via `skip = ["script/archives/**"]`. They cannot be run even by explicit path: `forge script script/archives/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:VerifyPromotionReady --rpc-url $RPC_MAINNET` -> `Error: Could not find target contract`, EXIT=1.

Two aggravating facts. First, `promotion-ready:verify` was created by story 075 specifically to remediate fix-pending Medium `2c53e944caee...` ("A broadcast run performs ZERO on-chain verification of its own outcome"); deleting it removes the accepted fix for a finding a human marked fix-pending, and no story authorises the removal — the purge of ~246 package.json keys has no story anywhere in the tree. Second, the cutover has ALREADY broadcast to mainnet: commit 4e5cca1 landed live addresses and `broadcast/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol/1/run-latest.json` is tracked. So `:verify` and `:resume` are not hypothetical future tooling — they are the post-hoc verification and recovery path for a migration that is live.

The wider stranding is quantified: 246 keys were deleted in this delta, and 81 live (open or fix-pending) ledger findings had their `entryPoint` deleted by it — including 23 open + 2 fix-pending on `promotion-ready:broadcast`, 3 on `:verify`, 4 on `:resume`, 1 on `:dry`, plus the whole ys-swap and migration-saga families. Their code survives under `script/archives/` but is uncompilable, so neither PoC replay nor `/recheck` has any path to re-prove or retire them.
impact: An operator following the surviving in-repo runbook is told to run three commands, two of which no longer exist and cannot be reinstated by path. The verification step for a migration already executed on mainnet is gone, reopening the exposure story 075 closed. And 81 live findings are frozen in an unresolvable state — not fixed, not abandoned, simply unreachable by the verification tooling. No direct on-chain loss, which caps this at Medium, but it degrades the project's ability to detect or recover from a bad mainnet cutover.
attackPath: 1. Delta 1d8a3a7..f929b5b deletes 246 package.json script keys (287 -> 41) and sweeps 108 files into script/archives/**.
2. The surviving in-repo runbook still instructs the operator to run three promotion-ready commands; two no longer exist and cannot be reinstated by path because skip makes them uncompilable.

3. The cutover those commands verify HAS ALREADY BROADCAST to mainnet (broadcast/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol/1/run-latest.json is tracked), so the exposure story 075 closed is reopened with no verification and no resume path.
4. 81 live ledger findings attributable to this delta (90 total lacking a surviving entry-point key) are frozen: not fixed, not abandoned, with no /recheck or PoC-replay path.
recommendation: Restore at minimum `promotion-ready:verify` and `promotion-ready:resume` (keys and compilable scripts) — the cutover they cover is already live on mainnet and `:verify` is the accepted fix for fix-pending `2c53e944caee`. For the rest, decide deliberately rather than by sweep: either keep the entry point and its script compiling, or delete the key AND its orphaned doc comment together, and retire the corresponding ledger findings explicitly (`/ledger ... abandon`) rather than leaving them stranded. If `script/archives/**` must stay in `skip`, add a CI check that every path referenced by a surviving package.json key or shell script resolves to a compilable target.
evidence: `git show 1d8a3a7:package.json` vs HEAD (key diff, 246 deletions); package.json:45-46 and the surviving `//promotion-ready`, `//migration-saga`, `//phlimbo-v1-to-v2` comments; foundry.toml:26-32; `forge script script/archives/VerifyPromotionReady.s.sol:VerifyPromotionReady` -> `Could not find target contract`, EXIT=1; `git ls-files broadcast/DeployMainnetPromotionReady.s.sol/1/run-latest.json`; ledger entryPoint tally against reports/phoenix-phase-2-staging/ledger.json.

classification.likelihood: certain - the state already exists at HEAD; the mainnet cutover is already live.
classification.assumptions: That verification and resume capability for a live mainnet cutover has operational value. `abandoned` explicitly does NOT apply here: the code is on master and merged, nobody chose to live with these findings, so marking them abandoned would bury live bugs.
classification.externalRequirements: A future incident, audit or resume attempt on the live cutover is what converts this latent loss into concrete harm.

severityRationale: Medium: no direct asset loss (which is the whole reason it is not High), but the protocol's ability to detect and recover from a bad mainnet cutover is materially degraded, and a human-accepted remediation for a still-open fix-pending Medium was removed by an untagged sweep. Stranding 81 live findings with no verification path is a Law-1 recall hazard in its own right. Escapes the local-chain ceiling outright: the code it concerns is live on mainnet.
severityNote: Proposed medium; CONFIRMED medium. Considered High and rejected: no asset path and no attacker - the harm is loss of assurance and recovery capability, not loss of funds.

dedupReasoning: CONSOLIDATION CANDIDATE CONSIDERED AND REJECTED against DEV28-09. Both descend from the same untagged script/archives sweep, but: (a) severity differs (Medium vs Low) — this one removes the accepted remediation for fix-pending Medium 2c53e944caee for a cutover ALREADY broadcast to mainnet, and strands 81 live ledger findings whose entryPoint was deleted; DEV28-09 is a dead local verification harness; (b) remediations are disjoint — restore npm keys + make the scripts compile + explicitly retire stranded findings, vs repoint two paths in a shell script and correct a false foundry.toml comment; (c) fixing either leaves the other live. Rule "keep both when severity implications differ and separate mitigation is required" governs. The shared origin is preserved as a relatedFindings edge to DEV28-11 rather than by merging. Also: this finding names fix-pending Medium 2c53e944caee, which lives on a DIFFERENT entryPoint (promotion-ready:*) — run rule 2 forbids collapsing across entry points, so it is cited, not merged.

ownerTriage.scopeBasis: The audited entry point was `dev` (package.json:16), which runs clean:local, anvil, deploy:local, simulate-yield.sh, extract:addresses, generate:ts-anvil and serve against chain 31337 only. This finding is anchored at package.json:45-46, the promotion-ready:* mainnet cutover block. No call chain, import or shared state connects them; the finding entered the run only because package.json is in the `dev` closure (that is where `dev` is defined) and the 1d8a3a7..f929b5b delta deleted 246 keys in that same file.
ownerTriage.recallNote: The orphaned-runbook half is a real defect that survives this disposal and belongs to the promotion-ready:* entry point. Because entryPoint is folded into the fingerprint, filing it there mints a DIFFERENT hash, so this wont-fix does not suppress it. The stranded-ledger half (81 open/fix-pending entries whose entryPoint key was deleted) is an observation about the audit repo's own ledger, not the audited code, and stays an open manual-review item for this repo.
